video_title: Stephen A. says Harden's comments 'don't make for a winning formula' 🚫🏆 | First Take

quotes.speaker: James Harden
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's self-assessment of his playoff performance
quotes.excerpt: I think I did pretty good. I don't grade myself off shot making. Defensively, been extremely solid.
quotes.quote: I think I did pretty good, you know. Like I don't even I don't grade myself off shot making. You know, I think coming here was just a piece to fulfill whatever needs to be fulfilled and, you know, defensively been extremely solid. Offensively, you know, getting guys shots and fitting into a system that was already in place. You know, so I think I did I think I did good. You know, obviously I could have been better. I feel like I always could be better, you know. But I know one thing that I work extremely hard.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on James Harden's declining playoff stats
quotes.excerpt: Conference Finals, 16 points, 39% from the field, 18% from three-point range.
quotes.quote: In the first round series against the Raptors, he averaged 20 on 45% shooting, 38% from three. No problem there. Pistons, 19.6 points, 38% shooting, 29% from three. Conference Finals, 16 points, 39% from the field, 18% from three-point range. Eight clutch time games, three and five record. 35% shooting from the field, 20% shooting from three-point range, 50% shooting from the free throw line. This is James Harden in clutch time.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's comments don't make for a winning formula
quotes.excerpt: You never want to give the impression, 'It's all right' that I lost. You want to look and you want to see that it hurts you.
quotes.quote: If we going to sit up there and we going to get on Jaylen Brown, who won a championship two years ago and won an NBA Finals MVP two years ago, yet we're saying to him, yo, it's not the wisest thing in the world to say 24 hours after giving up a 3-1 lead and losing in the first round that this was your favorite season. We can't sit up there and let James Harden off the hook by sitting up there and talking about, you think you play pretty good when you all just got swept. And you know good and damn well that if you did more to help Donovan Mitchell in a manner that we would expect from a James Harden, even at this age, that it would have been a better scenario for you all. You were also on the court when you all lost a 22-point lead in the last seven minutes of Game 1. And so you just look at it and you find yourself flabbergasted. If not flabbergasted, J, you know what it really how it really hit you and where it really hit you at. You know, he's got a player option that's going to pay him 42 million. And one of the things that we try to impart upon you know they talk about the media narrative and all of this stuff. This is what we try to tell them. Yo, there's an audience out there that we're talking to that speaks to us, they call in the radio shows, they call in the television shows, they tweet in and all of this stuff. Let you know where they stand and how they feel. You never want to give the impression, 'It's all right' that I lost. You if you're a fan, you want to look and you want to see that it hurts you just as more than it hurts the fan. And when you hear stuff like that, you just get the impression, 'Oh well, it happens, that's how it goes and that's that.' It's just not a it's not a great thing for him to say. It's not the end of the world, you understand, because it is what it is, but it doesn't make for a winning formula.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's age vs. commitment and conditioning
quotes.excerpt: I'm talking about the commitment, conditioning, taking care of yourself.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: I'm glad you all the both of you all are on the screen when I say what I'm about to say. James Harden is 36 years of age. He turns 38, I'm sorry, he turns 37 in August. Steph Curry is 38 years of age. 38. Are we looking at him getting old?

text_blocks.speaker: Cam Newton
text_blocks.text: But I said that in another segment, Stephen A.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: What I'm saying, what I'm getting to is, listen to where I'm going, Jay. I'm not bringing up game. This is not about game. I'm talking about the commitment, conditioning, taking care of yourself. LeBron 41. Why are we looking here wondering about what he's going to do and what the Lakers should do? Because all of this stuff, you all threw everything at Luka Doncic. Luka Doncic is the man, Luka Doncic is this, Luka Doncic is that. The brother 26, 27 years of age. Who was playing in the playoffs? And who wasn't? It was LeBron that was playing. It was Luka that wasn't. So in other words, when we look at cats getting old, understand, they're not necessarily just getting old. There's a level of commitment that appears to be lacking because your game is a game. Jay, I watched this, you and I've talked about this on many occasions when you've debated with me and on rare occasions you actually concede I have a good point. When I bring this up to you, Jay, I said there's a difference between getting ready and staying ready. When we look at those superstars, they don't come into the season and use the season to get ready. They come into the season ready. Now, they may upgrade and be even more ready as the season progresses, but they're ready from tip off. They're ready once it starts because their whole stuff is, 'We ain't going out like that. We the marquee.'

text_blocks.text: Harden in four Conference Finals games against the Knicks, 12 assists. Didn't he say he was passing the ball? Didn't he say passing the ball? Getting guys shots. Mikal Bridges, 83% when guarded by James Harden. 10 of 12. What are we talking about?

text_blocks.speaker: Jay Williams
text_blocks.text: I brought up analytics because the coach, that's what the coach is going to look at. The coach is going to look at analytics.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Disbelief at James Harden's self-assessment after playoff sweep
quotes.excerpt: This is a 36-year-old player who's been in the league for at least 15 years.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: I say to people, I'm brilliant because I know I'm not. I listen to those who are and I'm and I don't mind being a bit deferential. You see, this is one of the things that pisses me off when I'm on national television and cats try to come at me. They act like I'm the only one that says something. 12, 15 different people said it. Hall of Famers, former players, present players, but I say it and oh, I'm the one that's putting this out there. No. These are facts. This is what we're talking about. Now that man said, 'I was extremely solid defensively.' Those were his words. His words. This is a 36-year-old player who's been in the league for at least 15 years. You understand? He's he's pretty damn experienced at press conferences now. You're sitting up there and you're talking about, yo, this is what I did. Really? I mean, all we got to do is I the one thing that I am an expert at is clicking the remote control. I got DVR by the way. You understand? I ain't got one of them TVs that you can't rewind. You understand? I tape. I rewind. I watch, watch, watch, watch, watch. And I'm sitting there like this, 'What did he say?' You understand? Because you know that's what I did last night. No, no, no, hold on, wait a minute. I was sleepy. I was sleepy. You all tired. I West Coast. We're getting up at 4:30. I was sleepy as hell. And I went like this, 'I woke up.' What? What did he just say? Click. Rewind that stuff for me right there. I'm looking at the, 'Oh hell to the no, I didn't just hear him say that.' 83% shooting by Mikal Bridges when guarded by James Harden. 56% shooting by Jalen Brunson when guarded by James Harden. Overall 60% defensive efficiency. James Harden.
